article.title: Chapter Notes: November 2026
article.author: Pinellas DSA
article.content: Hello again, comrade! It’s the November edition of the Pinellas DSA Chapter Notes! We know that you’re probably still processing the results from the election on Tuesday. A lot of the votes in which we were most invested, like Angie’s campaign for US Senate and Amendment 3 to the state constitution, didn’t go our way. And, Florida is in for another four years of the reactionary Republican leadership in Tallahassee. But it’s not all bad news. In fact… far from it . Pinellas DSA members watch as election results trickle in on November 3. Pinellas DSA member Lindsey Grove won her bid for St. Pete City Council District 6, meaning a quarter of the council is now in DSA hands for the next four years! Our Tampa DSA comrade Ashley Herrmann won her race for Florida House District 69, flipping the seat from Republican Danny Alvarez. Republicans lost 15 seats, as well as their supermajority, in the Florida State House. And, DSA-endorsed candidates won key races across the country, including Melat Kiros in Colorado, Rashida Tlaib and Donavan Mckinney in Michigan, Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania, and more. Even in defeat, we can point to the fact that Angie shocked all the pollsters and pundits coming within striking distance of Ashley Moody. Tuesday’s results show that millions of Floridians can be inspired to come out when candidates embrace true working-class politics, in a way that they simply won’t respond to milquetoast liberals. Even though Florida was home to several hundred thousand more registered Republicans in 2026 as compared to 2022, DSA member Angie Nixon still outperformed centrist liberal Val Demings by a considerable margin. The 2026 midterms are over. Politics doesn’t happen only once every two or four years, though. Our path to victory lies in doing the day-to-day, grassroots work of building the socialist movement in Pinellas County and across the planet, 365 days a year! Read on to learn more about what our chapter was up to over the last month, and what we have coming up next. October Highlights Members of Pinellas DSA, Tampa DSA, and Pasco-Hernando DSA gathered for our Second-Annual Tri-Chapter Social. Our members spoke to thousands of Pinellas residents in October — on doorsteps, on sidewalks, in the streets, and in front of polling locations — in support of multiple initiatives. First, there was the #NoOn3 campaign, which our Electoral Committee initiated in August to get the word out about the cuts coming to municipal governments if Amendment 3 passed. Our Ecosocialist Working Group also circulated a petition as part of the Public Power St. Pete campaign, with the goal of getting a public electrical utility on the ballot for 2028. Local elected official and Pinellas DSA member Richie Floyd hosted a town hall to discuss property taxes, the services funded by them, and the potential impacts of Amendment 3, which yielded a lot of insightful questions and discussion. We also hosted a ballot party for folks to get together, discuss what is on their ballot, and have conversations around less straightforward items like local and state amendments or judges. Stepping outside of the electoral realm, we also hosted the Second-Annual Tri-Chapter Social in Palm Harbor, allowing us to meet up and share food, drinks, and fun with members of Tampa DSA and Pasco-Hernando DSA. And, we tabled at Halloween on Central in St. Pete, where we were able to meet dozens of local progressives that expressed interest in joining our movement! It’s no wonder that Creative Loafing named the DSA ‘Best Inevitability’ this month as part of the 2026 Best of the Bay awards! CAMPAIGN UPDATE: Dump Duke As mentioned above, organizers with our Dump Duke campaign have been hard at work circulating an official petition to get public power on the ballot in St. Pete. Organizers hosted Poll-a-Thons, occupying spots in front of strategically-selected polling locations across the city, hoping to engage voters on the way to cast their ballots. Organizers also circulated the petition at Halloween on Central, helping bring this exciting campaign to even more of our neighbors. Learn more about the petition drive here CAMPAIGN LAUNCH: Apartheid Free Pinellas We’re excited to announce the upcoming launch of a new initiative for our chapter: Apartheid Free Pinellas , which is being managed by our International Solidarity Working Group. Apartheid Free Pinellas is aimed at local businesses in Pinellas County. Campaigners will conduct outreach, helping to raise awareness of common products that have been included on the Boycott, Divestments & Sanctions list, and sharing information about how to replace these products with BDS-compliant alternatives. Participating businesses can display Apartheid Free Pinellas collateral in their stores, letting the community know that it’s safe to shop without concern that you might be inadvertently supporting Israel’s genocide against the Palestinian people. More information will be forthcoming. If you’re interested in getting involved, the first Apartheid Free Pinellas campaign meeting is scheduled for next Wednesday (November 11) at 6:30pm. The meeting will be Zoom only; you can RSVP at the link below. RSVP for the meeting COMMITTEE LAUNCH: Growth & Development PDSA members ready to canvass our neighors. The socialist movement has seen immense growth across the US in 2026. But, if we want to build an organization that can deliver on our ambitious goals, we need to put in place the protocols and procedures that can ensure that we have a healthy, sustainable chapter. To that end, your PDSA comrades are exploring the idea of launching a new committee, focused on growing and developing our chapter into 2027 and beyond. Initiatives that could be overseen by the new Growth & Development Committee may include political education, outreach, text and phonebanking, and planning events aimed at increasing engagement and retaining members. If you’re interested, we’ll be hosting a Growth & Development Committee interest meeting on Thursday, November 12. Check the Discord as the meeting date gets closer for more info! CAMPAIGN UPDATE: Canvassing with the St. Pete Tenants Union PDSA Housing Working Group members conducting outreach to St. Pete tenants. Our Housing Working Group has been steadfastly plugging away over the last few months, working with the St. Pete Tenants Union to identify troubled apartment complexes throughout the city and canvassing to try and organize renters to fight back against the slumlords that own these properties. The Housing Working Group and SPTU have several canvasses scheduled in the next couple of weeks, including at the Osprey Pointe Apartments, the Reserve at Lake Pointe, and the Enclave at Sabal Pointe, among others. With consistent effort, we will secure the right for renters to collectively bargain with landlords to demand better conditions, fair rents, and an end to evictions! Check the Housing channel in Discord for information about upcoming canvasses, and to see how you can get involved in the fight for tenants’ rights! ANNOUNCEMENT: Pinellas DSA Chapter Convention We are holding the first-ever PDSA Chapter Convention next month! A chapter convention is an exciting opportunity for the local membership to reflect on the past twelve months, and also participate in democratic discussion and debate about what our organizing work should look like for the next year. This means electing a new Steering Committee in addition to voting on working group reauthorizations, campaign proposals, bylaws amendments, and other member resolutions. 2027 Steering Committee nominations will open at the November General Body Meeting this Sunday. The deadline for both nominations and resolution submissions will be Saturday, November 21st. The convention itself will take place on Saturday, December 5th from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The location will be announced soon, but it will be held here in Pinellas County. Please RSVP at the link below if you plan to attend. We will be ordering catering for lunch, so it’s important that we get a general headcount and make note of any dietary restrictions (vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, etc.). RSVP here for the PDSA Convention! Upcoming Events We have more than a dozen political events, working group meetings, and social outings scheduled in November.
